{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — RadialSpark Consulting Agreement (Clear Capital as Customer)

**To:** Deal team 
**From:** In-house counsel 
**Re:** Playbook review — verified findings and redline positions

---

## 1. Executive summary

We reviewed the Agreement against the playbook and verified 19 findings. Eleven clauses are compliant (several better than our preferred position), six are deviations requiring redline, and two rules are unmet because no usable clause exists.

The commercial architecture is favourable to us in the areas that often cause trouble: there is no exclusivity, no non-compete, no minimum purchase or take-or-pay commitment, no MFN, no liquidated damages or early-termination fee, no auto-renewal, and no audit right running against us. The licence grant of Contractor background material (§ 4(c)) sits above the fallback.

The risk is concentrated in the risk-allocation and exit provisions. Three critical items drive our position: (i) Section 7 is headed "Indemnification of Contractor" but contains **no operative indemnity language at all**, leaving us with no defence or indemnity for third-party IP infringement, breach of law, data or confidentiality breach, or wilful misconduct; (ii) Section 4(a) fragments ownership of the Works invoice-by-invoice with no present assignment and no interim licence, and the Agreement nowhere confirms we retain ownership of our own data and pre-existing materials; and (iii) the Section 7(a) cap's sole carve-out cross-refers to Paragraph 9 (the Independent Contractor clause), so the exception is inoperative and no carve-out survives for confidentiality, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, IP or indemnification. Layered on top, we have **no convenience-exit from an in-flight SOW**, no transition assistance or data-return mechanic, no conformance warranty (with implied warranties disclaimed at § 5(e)), Arizona governing law, and no cyber/privacy insurance for a vendor that will handle our data and access our systems.

Our redlines are targeted and, where the counterparty has already struck a mutual bargain (non-solicit, insurance, arbitration), we have made the smallest edit that reaches the fallback rather than reopening the clause.

---

## 2. Findings

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Position / redline |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | **Missing** | § 7 Limitations of Liability; Indemnification of Contractor | Insert Contractor indemnity as new § 7(d) for third-party IP infringement, breach of law, data/confidentiality breach and wilful misconduct, with notice/control/cooperation mechanics and carve-out from the § 7 limitations. |
| 2 | Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | **Deviation** | § 4 Ownership of Materials Related to Services; Acceptance | Works to vest in Company by present assignment on creation (not conditioned on invoicing/payment); add sentence confirming Company retains ownership of its data and pre-existing materials. § 4(b) and 4(c) unchanged. |
| 3 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Cap, mutuality and carve-outs | **Deviation** | § 7 Limitations of Liability; Indemnification of Contractor | Mutual cap at greater of 12 months' fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000; standard uncapped Excluded Claims; confirm fee payment obligations are not capped damages. |
| 4 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | **Deviation** | § 10 (Nonassignability) | Add affiliate/successor carve-out for Company; bar Contractor assignment to a Company competitor; mutual reasonable-consent standard otherwise intact. No change-of-control trigger exists (acceptable). |
| 5 | High | T4C — Termination for convenience | **Deviation** | § 6 Termination | Add Company right to terminate the Agreement or any SOW on 30 days' notice with refund of prepaid fees for Services not performed. Mutual 15-day no-SOW right left intact. |
| 6 | High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Compliant | § 1 Purpose of Engagement | No exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation; task-by-task engagement under separate SOWs. Preferred position; no redline. |
| 7 | High | LD — Liquidated damages / penalties on Customer | Compliant | § 6 Termination | Accrued fees and expenses only on termination; no kill fee, minimum fee or early-termination charge. Preferred position; no redline. |
| 8 | High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Compliant | § 13 / § 4 | No covenant not to compete and no field-of-use restriction on Clear Capital. Preferred position; no redline. |
| 9 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 3 Contractor's Compensation | No audit, inspection or verification right over Clear Capital; better than preferred. Apply preferred limits if a records right is later added by SOW. |
| 10 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | **Deviation** | § 11 | Change Arizona to New York law; add exclusive New York County venue for proceedings not resolved by arbitration. Arbitration clause preserved (US-administered; not walk-away). |
| 11 | Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation | Compliant | § 3 Contractor's Compensation | No MFN, benchmarking or price-matching obligation on Customer. Preferred position; no redline. |
| 12 | Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum commitments / volume | Compliant | § 3 Contractor's Compensation | Time-and-materials only, fees payable for services actually ordered and performed. Preferred position; no redline. |
| 13 | Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | **Deviation** | § 13 | Add customary general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs only; duration (1 year) and scope untouched at fallback level. |
| 14 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Compliant | § 1 / § 6(a) | No auto-renewal; 15-day exit when no SOW outstanding. Meets, and on exit exceeds, preferred position. |
| 15 | Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | **Missing** | § 6 Termination | Insert new § 6(d): up to six months' transition assistance at then-current rates, return of data/Works/Confidential Information within 30 days in machine-readable format, certified deletion thereafter (90 days' assistance acceptable at fallback). |
| 16 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | **Deviation** | § 5 Contractor's Representations and Warranties and Warranty Disclaimer | Add express 90-day conformance warranty for Services and Works with re-performance, repair/replacement or refund; confirm express warranties survive the § 5(e) disclaimer. |
| 17 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | **Deviation** | § 7, para 14 | Add cyber/privacy liability limb at USD 5,000,000 where Contractor processes Company data (USD 2,000,000 offered as landing zone). Existing workers' comp, CGL and E&O limbs unchanged. |
| 18 | Low | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Compliant | § 4(c) | Royalty-free, non-exclusive, perpetual, sublicensable licence with broad modification rights; above fallback. No redline. |

---

## 3. Walk-away items

1. **Absence of any Contractor indemnity (§ 7 — INDEMN, missing).** Searches for "indemnif", "hold harmless" and "defend" return only the Section 7 heading; Section 7 consists solely of liability caps, a consequential damages waiver and an attorneys' fees waiver. The § 5(c) non-infringement warranty is not a defence or indemnity obligation. This fails even the fallback and sits in walk-away territory. Our insertion at § 7(d) must be carved out of the § 7 limitations, otherwise the fees-paid cap and attorneys' fee waiver neutralise it.
2. **No cyber/privacy insurance (§ 7, para 14 — INSURANCE).** The fallback requires E&O of USD 1M *and* cyber of USD 2M. Cyber is absent entirely for a vendor that, under § 8, receives Company data and records and, under § 1(c), works at our facilities and accesses our systems. This fails the fallback on a material term and approaches the walk-away concern.

**Adjacent but not walk-away:** the § 7(a) cap's carve-out cross-refers to Paragraph 9 (Independent Contractor) and is therefore inoperative, leaving confidentiality, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, IP and indemnification fully capped; and § 4(a)'s payment-conditioned, invoice-by-invoice vesting leaves work we commissioned owned by Contractor for any unbilled, unpaid or disputed period. Both sit below the fallback and both must be fixed. The mandatory arbitration clause is **not** walk-away territory — it is US-administered with confirmation in US courts.

---

## 4. Next steps

1. **Issue the redline** on the six deviations and two missing items, in the priority order: indemnity (new § 7(d)), liability carve-outs and cap basis (§ 7(a)–(c)), IP vesting and Customer Data ownership (§ 4(a), § 4(d)), then convenience termination (§ 6), transition and data return (new § 6(d)), warranty (§ 5), assignment (§ 10), governing law (§ 11), non-solicit carve-outs (§ 13) and cyber insurance (§ 7, para 14).
2. **Flag the drafting error** in the § 7(a) exception (cross-reference to Paragraph 9) to counterparty counsel as a correction rather than a negotiation, alongside the mismatch between the § 7 heading and its content.
3. **Signal fallback landing zones** where we have them: 90 days' transition assistance in place of six months; USD 2,000,000 cyber cover in place of USD 5,000,000; Delaware, California or England and Wales if New York is resisted; 90-day software / 30-day services warranty periods if the conformance warranty is contested.
4. **Hold firm** on the two walk-away items and on the liability carve-outs; the indemnity and the carve-out sentence should be treated as a single package, since neither works without the other.
5. **Note for the deal team** two uncapped-pricing points we are not redlining under these rules: § 3(b) permits Contractor to change rates on 30 days' notice with no uplift cap (mitigated by our 15-day no-SOW exit), and § 4(d) defers our right to modify the software until payment in full. Confirm whether either needs commercial escalation.
6. **Diligence item:** if any Statement of Work later introduces a records-examination right against us, apply the preferred audit limits (once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, at Contractor's cost) at that point."}
